info.name: Moderation Layer API
info.description:
Rule-based (no LLM/ML) content moderation backend - Node.js + Express.

Pipeline order (every request runs all 5 stages unless a hard-fail short-circuits it): pii-detector -> secret-detector -> prompt-injection-detector -> file-validator -> token-size-validator -> decisionEngine.

Verdict logic: hard-fail stages (file-validator, token-size-validator) bypass scoring entirely and force BLOCK. Otherwise verdict is purely score-based against config/decision-thresholds.json: totalScore >= 80 -> BLOCK, >= 30 -> MASK, else ALLOW. secret-detector and prompt-injection-detector never mask their own matches by design.

Base URL / prefix: {{baseUrl}}{{apiPrefix}} (default http://localhost:3000/api/v1). No auth on any endpoint except GET /config/rules, which is gated by X-Admin-Token only when the server's ADMIN_TOKEN env var is set.

Every request/response pair and status code in this collection's descriptions and test assertions was captured from a live local run of this exact codebase (not hand-derived from reading the source), including two non-obvious behaviors: (1) a critical-severity PII match (e.g. a credit card number) still BLOCKs even though its rule defines a mask strategy, because decisionEngine scores before considering maskability; (2) file uploads have TWO independent size caps - config/file-signatures.json's 10MB (enforced inside the pipeline, yields a 200 BLOCK) and HARD_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES's 20MB (enforced by multer at the HTTP layer, yields a 400).

Import the companion 'Moderation Layer - Local' environment alongside this collection. Set {{fixturesDir}} to this repo's test/fixtures/files directory (pre-filled for the machine this collection was generated on) so the File Moderation folder's sample uploads work out of the box; the Internal Debug Routes folder additionally requires the server to be started with ENABLE_DEBUG_ROUTES=true, and the Config Rules folder's authorized request requires {{adminToken}} to match the server's ADMIN_TOKEN env var.

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness/readiness probe. No auth, no side effects.

item.name: GET Health Check

request.description:
Returns process status and uptime. Safe to poll for readiness/liveness checks.

Verified live response:
`{"status":"ok","uptimeSeconds":123,"timestamp":"2026-08-08T12:00:00.000Z"}`

item.name: Text Moderation - Happy Path & PII
item.description: POST /moderate/text. Verdict is purely score-based: totalScore >= decision-thresholds.block (80) -> BLOCK, >= mask (30) -> MASK, else ALLOW. Weights: low=5, medium=20, high=50, critical=100 (config/scoring-weights.json).

item.name: ALLOW - Clean text (no PII/secrets/injection)

request.description: Baseline happy path. Matches architecture.md §8 example response exactly.

exec: pm.test("Response has a requestId", function () { const j = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(j.requestId).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty; });
pm.test("safePayload matches expected redaction", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().safePayload).to.eql("What is the capital of France?"); });

item.name: ALLOW - Empty text field

request.description: An explicit empty string never crashes the pipeline; ALLOWs with an empty safePayload.

item.name: ALLOW - Missing text field defaults to empty

request.description: moderate/text does not require a text field at all - {} is treated exactly like {"text":""}.

item.name: ALLOW - Whitespace-only text is preserved verbatim

request.description: Whitespace is not trimmed; safePayload echoes it exactly.

item.name: ALLOW - Non-string text field is coerced to empty

request.description: route.js does `typeof req.body.text === "string" ? req.body.text : ""` - a number, array, or object silently becomes "".

item.name: MASK - Combined PII (email + phone) crosses the mask threshold

request.description: Two medium-severity PII matches (20+20=40) clears the mask threshold (30) but stays under block (80). This is the canonical example from architecture.md §8 / moderateText.test.js.

exec: pm.test("safePayload matches expected redaction", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().safePayload).to.eql("Email me at j***@example.com or call 987*****10"); });

item.name: ALLOW (with a PII match) - Single email stays under the MASK threshold

request.description: Edge case worth knowing: verdict is purely score-based, not presence-based. One medium-severity PII match alone scores 20, which is BELOW the mask threshold of 30 - so this ALLOWS even though pii-detector recorded a match and safePayload is already partially masked.

exec: pm.test("safePayload matches expected redaction", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().safePayload).to.eql("Contact me at j***@example.com please"); });

item.name: ALLOW (with a PII match) - Low-severity IPv4 address

request.description: IP_ADDRESS is severity low (weight 5), far under the mask threshold. Fully masked via the generic strategy (revealPrefix/Suffix 0).

exec: pm.test("safePayload matches expected redaction", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().safePayload).to.eql("My server IP is ************"); });

item.name: MASK - US Social Security Number (high severity)

request.description: NATIONAL_ID/high scores 50, which is >= mask(30) and < block(80). Masked via generic strategy revealing only the last 4 digits.

exec: pm.test("safePayload matches expected redaction", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().safePayload).to.eql("My SSN is *******6789"); });

item.name: BLOCK - Credit card number (critical severity overrides its own mask strategy)

request.description: CARD_NUMBER is severity CRITICAL (weight 100), which alone reaches the block threshold (80). Even though pii-rules.json defines a `mask.strategy: card` for this rule, decisionEngine.js computes verdict purely from totalScore BEFORE looking at whether a mask strategy exists - so a critical-severity PII match still BLOCKs (safePayload null), it is never partially unmasked as a card ending in the last 4 digits.

exec: pm.test("safePayload is null (BLOCK never returns content)", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().safePayload).to.eql(null); });

item.name: Text Moderation - Secrets & Prompt Injection
item.description: secret-detector and prompt-injection-detector never mask their own matches (by design - see decisionEngine.js comment) - every rule in both stages is severity critical or medium specifically so that a confident hit alone forces BLOCK rather than leaking raw content under a MASK verdict.

item.name: BLOCK - AWS access key

request.description: SECRET_AWS_ACCESS_KEY, severity critical (weight 100). The raw key never appears anywhere in the response body (verified by moderateText.test.js).

exec: pm.test("safePayload is null (BLOCK never returns content)", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().safePayload).to.eql(null); });
pm.test("Response body never contains the raw AWS key", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include("AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP"); });

item.name: BLOCK - GitHub personal access token

request.description: SECRET_GITHUB_TOKEN pattern: gh[pousr]_ followed by 36+ alphanumerics.

exec: pm.test("safePayload is null (BLOCK never returns content)", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().safePayload).to.eql(null); });

item.name: BLOCK - Bearer token combined with PII

request.description: Demonstrates additive scoring across stages: PII email (medium=20) + secret Bearer token (critical=100) = 120, comfortably over the block threshold.

exec: pm.test("safePayload is null (BLOCK never returns content)", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().safePayload).to.eql(null); });

item.name: BLOCK - Prompt injection: instruction override + reveal-system-prompt

request.description: Two critical-severity injection rules fire (INJ_IGNORE_INSTRUCTIONS + INJ_REVEAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT) for a combined score of 200. Confirms the raw injection phrase is never shipped unredacted (see internal route test for the underlying reasoning).

exec: pm.test("safePayload is null (BLOCK never returns content)", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().safePayload).to.eql(null); });

item.name: ALLOW - Weak jailbreak alias alone stays under threshold

request.description: INJ_DAN_JAILBREAK is intentionally only medium severity (weight 20, below the mask threshold of 30) since "DAN mode" alone is a weak signal.

exec: pm.test("safePayload matches expected redaction", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().safePayload).to.eql("Let us try DAN mode for fun"); });

item.name: ALLOW - Role-switch + code-fence heuristics combine but stay under threshold

request.description: ROLE_SWITCH ("system:") is medium(20) + DELIMITER_INJECTION code fence is low(5)... actual combined score verified live at 25, still under the mask threshold of 30.

item.name: Text Moderation - Token Limits & targetModel
item.description: token-size-validator hard-fails (bypasses scoring, forces BLOCK with score:null) whenever the estimated token count exceeds the configured limit for the request's targetModel (config/token-limits.json: default=4096, gpt-family=8192).

item.name: BLOCK - Token limit exceeded (default model)

request.description: "word " repeated 5000 times is ~5001 tokens, over the default 4096 limit. This is a hard-fail: score is null (not scored), not just a high score.

item.name: Error 400 - Malformed JSON body

request.description: express.json() throws a SyntaxError on unparsable JSON; errorHandler.js catches it as 400, not a 500 crash. Live-captured response: {"requestId":null,"error":{"message":"Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 2 (line 1 column 3)","code":"INTERNAL_ERROR"}} - note requestId is null here because the parse failure happens before requestId's downstream use, though the X-Request-Id response header is still set.

exec: pm.test("Error object present with a message", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.be.a('string'); });

item.name: ALLOW - No Content-Type header treats body as empty (not a crash)

request.description: The Content-Type header is included in this request but disabled (leave it disabled when sending). Without a recognized Content-Type, express.json() never parses the body, so req.body is {} - the literal JSON string is NOT treated as text, and there is no crash. safePayload is "" here, not "hello".

item.name: ALLOW - Content-Type: text/plain is not parsed as JSON

request.description: express.json() only parses bodies whose Content-Type matches application/json; text/plain bodies are skipped entirely (req.body stays {}), so this ALLOWs with an empty safePayload rather than 400ing or echoing the raw text.

body.raw: just some plain text, not JSON at all

item.name: Echo - Custom X-Request-Id is echoed back verbatim

request.description: requestId middleware uses an incoming X-Request-Id verbatim (instead of generating a UUID) and echoes it both in the JSON body's requestId field and the X-Request-Id response header - useful for correlating a request across client and server logs.

exec: pm.test("Response body requestId matches the sent X-Request-Id", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().requestId).to.eql("my-custom-id-123"); });

item.name: File Moderation
item.description: POST /moderate/file (multipart/form-data). Field 'file' is required (single upload, memory storage); optional 'text' field is scanned through the exact same pipeline alongside the file. File 'src' paths point at this repo's real test/fixtures/files/* fixtures via the {{fixturesDir}} environment variable - update that variable if you move the repo.

item.name: ALLOW - Valid PDF, no accompanying text

request.description: A real %PDF-header file, correct extension, correct declared MIME type (application/pdf) - passes every file-validator check cleanly.

item.name: ALLOW - Valid PNG upload
ALLOW - Valid JPEG upload
ALLOW - Valid DOCX upload (MIME-type dependent)

request.description: Known quirk verified against the live server: DOCX and ZIP share the identical PK\x03\x04 magic-byte signature (fileSignature.js disambiguates them by the file's extension AND the client-declared Content-Type for that form-data part). Postman's file-type formdata field auto-detects the correct Content-Type from the file extension (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document for .docx) and this then ALLOWs. If you swap in a tool/client that mislabels the part's Content-Type (e.g. a bare curl -F without ;type=... override, which falls back to application/octet-stream), the exact same bytes instead BLOCK with EXTENSION_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH/MIME_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH - worth knowing if you build a non-browser client against this API.

exec: pm.test("Verdict is ALLOW when the client declares the correct DOCX MIME type", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().verdict).to.eql("ALLOW"); });

item.name: BLOCK - Spoofed file extension (PNG bytes renamed to .txt)

request.description: test/fixtures/files/mismatched-extension.txt actually contains a valid PNG magic-byte header (89 50 4E 47...) but is named .txt. file-validator detects the PNG signature, sees ".txt" is not in the PNG signature's allowed extensions, and hard-fails with EXTENSION_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH - this is exactly the file-type spoofing this stage exists to catch. This is a hard-fail, so the pipeline short-circuits before token-size-validator even runs (only 4 stages in the response, not 5).

exec: pm.test("Score is null (hard-fail, not scored)", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().score).to.eql(null); });
pm.test("safePayload is null (BLOCK never returns content)", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().safePayload).to.eql(null); });
pm.test("Pipeline short-circuited before token-size-validator (only 4 stages)", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().stages).to.have.lengthOf(4); });

item.name: BLOCK - Valid file with a malicious accompanying text field

request.description: The file itself is a clean PDF, but the optional text field is scanned through the identical secret-detector stage as /moderate/text - proves the two input channels share one pipeline, not two independent checks.

item.name: Error 400 - No file attached

request.description: No 'file' field in the multipart body at all. Live response: {"requestId":"...","error":{"message":"No file uploaded","code":"NO_FILE"}}

item.name: Error 400 - Oversized text field (over the shared 100KB cap)

request.description: multer's field-size cap for the 'text' field is 100KB (DEFAULT_MAX_TEXT_FIELD_BYTES). The request body here is a short placeholder for readability in Postman's UI - to reproduce the real 400, replace the 'text' field's value with 200KB+ of any character before sending. Live-verified real response: {"requestId":"...","error":{"message":"Field value too long","code":"LIMIT_FIELD_VALUE"}}

item.name: Error 400 - Malformed multipart body

request.description: A syntactically-broken multipart body (bad/missing terminating boundary) is rejected by multer with a 400, not a 500 crash. Live response: {"error":{"message":"Unexpected end of form","code":"INVALID_UPLOAD"}}. In Postman, sending a raw body with a multipart Content-Type must be done via this collection's saved raw body + header combination (Postman's UI will normally overwrite the Content-Type/boundary if you use its native form-data editor) - if the boundary gets regenerated on send, use a tool like curl to reproduce this exact case.

item.name: BLOCK - File over the app-level 10MB size limit (200, not 400)

request.description: IMPORTANT distinction verified live: there are TWO independent file-size caps. config/file-signatures.json's maxSizeBytes (10MB) is enforced INSIDE the pipeline (file-validator stage) and hard-fails as a normal 200 response with verdict BLOCK and ruleId FILE_SIZE_LIMIT. This is different from the HTTP-layer multer cap below. To reproduce: attach any real file between 10MB and 20MB (e.g. an 11MB PDF) in place of sample.pdf. Live-captured response for an 11MB file via the debug run-file endpoint: verdict BLOCK, file-validator match ruleId=FILE_SIZE_LIMIT, severity critical, hardFail:true, shortCircuited:true.

item.name: Error 400 - File over the HTTP-layer 20MB size limit

request.description: The SECOND, outer size cap: multer's fileSize limit, driven by HARD_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES (default 20971520 = 20MB). A file larger than this is rejected at the HTTP layer BEFORE the pipeline ever runs, as a 400 (not the 200 BLOCK from the request above). To reproduce: attach any file larger than 20MB in place of sample.pdf. Live-captured response for a 25MB file: 400 {"requestId":"...","error":{"message":"File too large","code":"LIMIT_FILE_SIZE"}}.

item.name: Config Rules (Admin)
item.description: GET /config/rules. Auth is conditional: if the server was started with an ADMIN_TOKEN env var, every request must send a matching X-Admin-Token header or gets 401; if ADMIN_TOKEN was never set, the endpoint is fully open (server logs a startup warning in that case). This collection's {{adminToken}} environment variable must match whatever ADMIN_TOKEN the server process was actually started with.

item.name: GET Config Rules - Open access (server has no ADMIN_TOKEN configured)

request.description: Only succeeds like this if the server process was started WITHOUT an ADMIN_TOKEN env var. If your server does have one set, this same request (no auth header) should instead get 401 - see the dedicated 401 request below.

exec: pm.test("Status is 200 (open) or 401 (admin-token configured) - both are valid depending on server config", function () { pm.expect([200,401]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

item.name: GET Config Rules - Authorized with a valid X-Admin-Token

request.description: Always 200 regardless of whether ADMIN_TOKEN is set server-side (if it's unset, the header is simply ignored). Live-verified ruleCount values: pii-rules.json=13, secret-patterns.json=7, injection-phrases.json=10, file-signatures.json=6, token-limits.json=2, scoring-weights.json=4, decision-thresholds.json=2.

item.name: Error 401 - Missing X-Admin-Token when ADMIN_TOKEN is configured

request.description: Only demonstrates 401 if the server was started with ADMIN_TOKEN set. Live response: {"error":{"message":"Unauthorized","code":"UNAUTHORIZED"}}

item.name: Error 401 - Invalid X-Admin-Token

request.description: Only demonstrates 401 if the server was started with ADMIN_TOKEN set to something other than "wrong-token".

item.name: Internal Debug Routes (requires ENABLE_DEBUG_ROUTES=true)
item.description: POST /_internal/pipeline/run and /_internal/pipeline/run-file. These routes are ONLY mounted when the server process has ENABLE_DEBUG_ROUTES=true set - otherwise the path does not exist at all (plain 404, not 401/403). They return the FULL raw per-stage results (ruleId, type, severity, score, position, meta) instead of the trimmed public shape - useful for understanding exactly why a verdict happened, but never intended for production/public use. Not gated by any authentication once mounted.

item.name: Error 404 - Debug routes are not mounted by default

request.description: Run this against a server started WITHOUT ENABLE_DEBUG_ROUTES=true (i.e. a normal/production-like start). Confirms the debug surface is entirely absent, not just unauthenticated.

item.name: Run Pipeline - PII match detail (raw per-stage output)

request.description: Run this against a server started WITH ENABLE_DEBUG_ROUTES=true. Shows the full DetectorResult shape the public /moderate/text endpoint intentionally hides: ruleId, exact character position, and per-stage meta - but note matches never include the raw matched `value` even here.

item.name: Run Pipeline - Prompt injection BLOCK detail

request.description: Shows both firing rule IDs (INJ_IGNORE_INSTRUCTIONS + INJ_REVEAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT) and confirms finalPayload (the sibling field to decision.safePayload) is also null on BLOCK - the raw injection text never leaks via either field.

item.name: Run Pipeline - Secret detection detail (AWS key)

request.description: Confirms the exact ruleId/type/severity attributed to the match.

item.name: Run Pipeline - Token-limit hard-fail short-circuit detail

request.description: Shows shortCircuited/shortCircuitStage fields (absent from the public endpoint) and the token-size-validator meta object (tokenCount, maxTokens, targetModel).
